# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-25 (Extended v176)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to spring Year 7. Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet (Valjean's house), Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire No. 6 (Gillenormand residence), Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of the Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue de l'Homme Armé, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, river crossing at Dungate, harbor town of Wilholt. English provincial towns: Ravenmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Staveford, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Kelford, Pontoise, Dungate, Torton, Quenford.

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: Yera Stenworth confided fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (winter Year 5). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald confided/revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (autumn Year 6).

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa later went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford, took lodgings in Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead, took lodgings in Salcombe; Fenelle Lindmere followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate, took lodgings in Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family (evening 24th June). Thizek Stenenridge told Elra Corrford deed to Kelmere pastures was forged (evening 24th June). Vesmira and Isvie bought and regretted ribbon purchases (evening 24th June).

**Spring Year 7 observations**: Isvie walked long way to avoid muddy square. Bremira Corrford and Isvie discussed weather, harvest, lame horse. Isvie Stenworth complained about salt prices; Thizek Stenenridge agreed. Thizek walked long way to avoid muddy square. At Dungate river crossing, vespers bell rang; gulls fought over fish heads. Taric Corrley remarked river was up; Kassa Stenson said it always was in spring. Taric Corrley bought ribbon, regretted it. Kassa Stenson's husband gave solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Kassa watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly. Road rutted and puddled after thaw. Someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall. Light came early.

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son named Movus Brackick; family lived in Wilholt. Movus and Kadrek discussed weather, harvest, lame horse. Rinelle discussed same topics with Movus. Rinelle hummed childhood tune while scrubbing step. Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; couple lived in Ostcombe thereafter. Zavus Prydenridge hummed childhood tune while scrubbing step. Movie Prydenridge walked long way to avoid muddy square. Islan Thornmere read almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints. Nerine read almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints. Cart with turnips passed well in Ostcombe.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis and Discovery (Night of 24th June 1832, continuing into Spring Year 7)
**Blotting-book discovery**: Upon arriving at Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings, Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book open on sideboard before mirror. When examined directly, reversed letters made no sense; when viewed in mirror reflection, they revealed four lines—a letter Cosette had written and given to young workman in Rue Plumet. **Valjean's collapse**: Understood instantly Cosette had written to someone else. Soul gave utter roar; Cosette was escaping, slipping like cloud and water; another was goal of her heart; he was no longer anything but her father, no longer existed.

**Nature of his paternal love**: Loved Cosette as father only—yet into this paternity his life's widowhood introduced all shades of love: daughter, mother, sister, woman, wife. Never having known family love, nature made sentiment impossible to lose—pure with blindness's purity, unconscious, celestial, angelic, divine. Destinies wedded though no marriage possible.

**Philosophical and spiritual collapse**: Confronted with proof another was her dearest, grief surpassed bounds of possibility. Quiver of revolt ran head to foot; in roots of hair, immense reawakening of egotism; the *I* howled. Inward subsoil gave way; profound elements crumbling—fatal crisis. **Divination**: Measured terrible step destiny took without suspicion. Recognized precipice—but was at bottom. Found man instantly without knowing name: unknown prowler of Luxembourg, seeker of love adventures, idler of romance, coward making eyes at young girl with devoted father. After verification, regenerated Jean Valjean, who labored to resolve all life into love, beheld spectre: Hate.

**During Spring Year 7**: Groped up stairs, hand trembling greatly; thought his actions smacked of theft. Lit candle with difficulty; unfolded Marius's note to Cosette. In violent emotions, one seizes essential points. In the note, saw only two lines—Marius announcing his death and love. **Valjean's transformation**: Remained crushed, staring at note with intoxicated amazement, beheld splendor: death of hated individual. **Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. Initially slept well; awoke in mood almost gay; recovered serenity and sense of security. Twice or thrice Toussaint stammered about fighting in Paris—he paid no heed, absorbed in calculations.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance (Autumn Year 5 through Evening 24th June 1832)
**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged she never forgot Marius, always loved him. Fire smoldered, burst afresh. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening, forcing old gate. At height of love's voluptuousness, remained absolutely chaste. **Confessions (spring Year 6, during cholera)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer living by writing, father colonel and hero on bad terms with rich grandfather, hinted at being baron. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent, very good, gave to poor. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of her death as blessing, put hand on gun muzzle to protect him. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; asked grandfather, he refused; she has no fortune, neither does Marius; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him; when he reads, her soul near, he will smile. **Marius's response**: Covered letter with kisses; reflected Cosette going to England, grandfather refuses marriage, nothing changed. Resolved to inform Cosette of death, send farewell, save Gavroche.

**Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, declared gravest atrocity, arranged meeting 26th June at nine o'clock. Same evening, displaced bar at grating, rushed in. Cosette absent from waiting spot. Searched garden; deserted. Seated self with heart filled with sweetness and resolution, blessed love, said all left was to die. Mad with grief, incapable of accepting fate after two months intoxication, overwhelmed by despair, one desire: speedy end. Voice summoned him to barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie. Traversed boulevard, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Champs-Élysées, Place Louis XV, Rue de Rivoli, Halles, Rue de la Poterie; received bullet wound near Rue du Contrat-Social; reached Rue Mondétour, perceived barricade interior at ten fathoms. **Raised eyes; splendid rectification in mind—war of street transfigured by inward working of soul.**

**Philosophy of duty**: Reflected on Colonel Pontmercy—proud soldier, guarded French frontier under Republic, touched Asia under Napoleon, beheld cities, left blood on battlefields, returned after twenty years scarred but pure. Own day come; must follow father, show bravery, run to meet bullets, offer breast to bayonets, shed blood, seek death. Carries loaded pistols from 3d February adventure.

**During first phase**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed, Courfeyrac shouting; all hesitation vanished. Flung self into conflict, saved Gavroche with first shot, delivered Courfeyrac with second. Seized powder barrel, took advantage of smoke, glided along barricade to cage of paving-stones where torch fixed, tore torch, replaced with powder barrel, thrust stones under it, staved in, stood foot on stones, torch in hand, haughty face illuminated by fatal resolution, dropped flame toward pile, gave startling cry. **Mental state**: Had furnace in brain; now whirlwind. Effect of being outside himself. Two luminous months ending at frightful precipice, Cosette lost, barricade, M. Mabeuf killed, self leader—tremendous nightmare. Did not recognize Javert bound to post.

## Barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie (Evening 24th June 1832, repaired and augmented into Spring Year 7)
**Café Corinthe**: Ground floor with bar; first floor with billiard-table and wooden spiral staircase; cellar via trap-door; lodgings and attics. Proprietor: Widow Hucheloup. Serving-maids: Matelote (large, plump, red-haired), Gibelotte (tall, delicate, white, lymphatic). **Two barricades**: Enjolras, Combeferre, Courfeyrac directed. Larger shut off Rue de la Chanvrerie; other closed Rue Mondétour. Interior: irregular square, twenty paces between grand barrier and lofty houses. Issue left free on Rue Mondétour opening to Halles.

**Larger barricade (evening 24th June)**: Height six or seven feet, stepped construction, paling-stones, casks, wheels, omnibus pole with ropes, red flag. Forty-three insurgents: Enjolras, Combeferre, Courfeyrac, Bossuet, Joly, Bahorel, Gavroche. Six commanded by Feuilly at windows with guns. Sentinels stationed. **Javert's arrest**: Identified as Inspector of Police, aged fifty-two. Card, watch, purse with gold, sealed envelope with five lines in Prefect's handwriting discovered.

**Le Cabuc execution**: Utter stranger examined house. Enjolras, pale, Greek-profile, expression wrath and chastity, executed him. Justified: man killed, I killed him; insurrection needs discipline; love glorified; future: no one kills anyone, earth beams. Tradition: Le Cabuc was Claquesous; left no trace.

**M. Mabeuf's sacrifice**: Venerable, austere, sold unique Diogenes Laertius, returned with hundred francs, seated motionless at dawn. Evening 24th June: followed band, step firm, refused arms, retreated into self at Corinthe. During attack: at detonation, started up, appeared on threshold as Enjolras appealed for volunteer. Tore flag from Enjolras, no one dared stop him. Eighty years old, white locks, aged arm upholding red banner rose through gloom, enlarged in bloody light. Enjolras eulogized: teaches young, we hesitated, he came, magnificent death; his presence renders barricade impregnable.

**Unknown young figure**: Pale, thin, small, freckled, youthful artisan in tattered blouse and patched velvet trousers; spoke to Courfeyrac in voice not womanly. During attack: soldier aimed at Marius; hand laid on muzzle, obstructed it. Shot traversed hand, artisan possibly struck, fell, but ball did not hit Marius. Marius hardly noticed through smoke.

**After first assault and repairs (into Spring Year 7)**: Insurgents surprised but not terrified, rallied. Majority ascended to first-story window, commanded assailants. Medical students cared for wounded. Thrown tables out except two for lint and cartridges and one with Father Mabeuf; added to barricade; replaced with mattresses for wounded. Three poor creatures found in cellar. Assailants did not stir; marching heard but did not venture in. **Further augmentation**: Under Enjolras's eye, Marius no longer looking after anything, barricade not only repaired but augmented. Raised two feet. Bars of iron planted in pavement resembled lances in rest. All sorts of rubbish brought and added from all directions complicated external confusion. Redoubt cleverly made over, into wall on inside and thicket on outside. Tap-room disencumbered, kitchen appropriated for ambulance, dressing of wounded completed, powder scattered on ground and tables gathered up, bullets run, cartridges manufactured, lint scraped, fallen weapons redistributed, interior cleaned, rubbish swept up, corpses removed.

## Gavroche's Activities (Evening 24th June 1832, Spring Year 7)
**Evening 24th June**: After staring in air, stared below; raised self on tiptoes, felt doors and windows of ground floor; all shut, bolted, padlocked. After authenticating five or six barricaded houses, shrugged shoulders, took himself to task. Later, took himself off, fluttered away direction whence come, plunged back into gloom, rigid rapidity of projectile; Rue de l'Homme Armé became silent; strange child buried self in mists of black houses, lost like smoke in dark. Minutes after disappearance, startling shiver of glass; magnificent crash of lantern on pavement awakened indignant bourgeois. Gavroche in Rue du Chaume.

**Spring Year 7**: Broke lantern in Rue du Chaume, entered Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes; not seeing cat there, thought opportunity good to strike up song. March accelerated by singing. Sowed incendiary couplets along sleeping or terrified houses. Lavish of pantomime; face inexhaustible repertory of masks, produced grimaces more fantastic than torn cloth. Alone at night, neither seen nor visible—wastes of riches. **Perilous moment**: Post at Royal Printing Establishment occupied by National Guards of suburbs. Squad began waking, heads raised from camp beds. Two street lanterns broken in succession, ditty sung at top of lungs. For hour, boy created uproar in peaceable arrondissement. Sergeant of banlieue lent ear, waited, prudent man. **Cart incident**: When sergeant about to descend on Gavroche, cart converted into projectile, launched with might, rolled furiously down upon him; sergeant struck full in stomach, tumbled backwards into gutter, gun discharged in air. After panting, Gavroche turned toward fusillade, lifted left hand to nose level, thrust forward three times, slapped back of head with right hand—imperious gesture in which Parisian street-urchindom condensed French irony, efficacious, lasted half century. Post's recourse: Cart conquered, drunken man taken prisoner. First put in pound, second somewhat harassed before councils of war as accomplice. Public ministry proved indefatigable zeal in defence of society.

## Historical Note on June 1848 and the Barricade of Faubourg du Temple (Chapter 25)
Two most memorable barricades do not belong to period of action. Both symbols of redoubtable situation, sprang from earth at fatal insurrection of June 1848—greatest war of streets history beheld. Philosophy: exasperations of crowd which suffers and bleeds, violences contrary to all sense, directed against principles which are its life, are its popular coups d'état and should be repressed. Man of probity sacrifices himself, and out of very love for crowd, he combats it. But how excusable he feels it even while holding out against it! How he venerates it even while resisting it! One persists, it is necessary, but conscience, though satisfied, is sad, and accomplishment of duty complicated with pain at heart.

**June 1848 exceptional**: Revolt of people against itself. Attacked in name of revolution what? The revolution. Barricade, chance, hazard, disorder, terror, misunderstanding, unknown had facing it Constituent Assembly, sovereignty of people, universal suffrage, nation, republic. Carmagnole biding defiance to Marseillaise. Faubourg and redoubt lent each other assistance. Vast barricade spread out like cliff against which strategy of African generals dashed itself. Caverns, excrescences, warts, gibbosities grimaced and grinned beneath smoke. Mitraille vanished in shapelessness; bombs plunged into it; bullets only made holes in it. Regiments accustomed to fiercest visions of war gazed with uneasy eyes on species of redoubt, wild beast in boar-like bristling and mountain by enormous size.

**Barricade of Faubourg du Temple**: Defended by eighty men, attacked by ten thousand, held out three days. On fourth, pierced houses, came over roofs, barricade taken. Not one of eighty thought of flight, all killed except leader Barthélemy. Cournet was man of lofty stature, broad shoulders, red face, crushing fist, bold heart, loyal soul, sincere and terrible eye. Intrepid, energetic, irascible, stormy; most cordial of men, most formidable of combatants. War, strife, conflict were very air he breathed and put him in good humor. Former naval officer; from gestures and voice, one divined he sprang from ocean, came from tempest; carried hurricane into battle. With exception of genius, something of Danton in Cournet; with exception of divinity, something of Hercules in Danton.

**Later fatal circumstance**: In London, proscribed by all, Barthélemy slew Cournet in funereal duel. Some time afterwards, caught in gearing of mysterious adventures in which passion played part, catastrophe in which French justice sees extenuating circumstances and English justice sees only death, Barthélemy hanged. Sombre social construction so made that, thanks to material destitution and moral obscurity, that unhappy being who possessed intelligence, certainly firm, possibly great, began in France with galleys and ended in England with gallows. Barthélemy, on occasion, flew but one flag, black flag.

**Sixteen years context**: Sixteen years count in subterranean education of insurrection; June 1848 knew great deal more about it than June 1832. Barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie was only outline and embryo compared to two colossal barricades; but formidable for that epoch.
